npcs/isolde.title: Isolde
npcs/isolde.content:
Leader of the vampire coven at Harlan’s farm. She was once handmaiden to the governess Celandine, and is Celandine’s sister. She was Henrietta’s partner of ten years.

Twelve years ago she vanished without a word, around the time the governess died. Henrietta has been waiting for her ever since. In Odettia’s vision (S25), seen through Isolde’s own eyes, the governess lay murdered in a torchlit dungeon.
The coven. She arrived at Harlan’s farm frightened and on the run, carrying only a tapestry of two crowned women. Laura hid her and her coven in the cellar for twelve years. They lived on animals and weekly bottled blood from the harbour.
Harlan. When Harlan beat Laura, Isolde asked her, “Do you want me to take care of this?”, then killed him. She told Laura the last human she had wanted to kill was the old governor.
S26. She watched her coven attack Osric, bit Odettia, was knocked out by Vander and spared. She claimed her coven hunts “a greater evil” in the manor that wears a familiar face, offered a guarded truce, and left as mist.
S27, in the orchard with Quinn:

“They killed my sister in front of me.” She holds everyone in the manor complicit.
She wants a life with Henrietta, but the town hunts her every night.
She offered to release Odettia’s bite in exchange for Celandine’s last letter.
She asked Quinn to let her into the manor, and doubts Leon is truly her nephew.
She will consult her coven before answering.



Appearance: an older, calm vampire with cold authority. In S27 she wore a grey, tattered dress.

npcs/laura.title: Laura
npcs/laura.content:
Harlan’s widow, a farmer’s wife in her fifties, married to him since eighteen.

S25: Vander found her locked upstairs at the farm. She tested him by cutting herself to see whether he hungered. She said a red-eyed, clawed woman had seized Harlan and spared her. Vander buried Harlan and brought her to the Green Leaf, where Kaelith found and healed bruises on her ribs, shoulders and neck. Harlan had been beating her.
S27, her confession (for 20 more gold in her bag):

She sheltered the vampire coven in her cellar for twelve years, made sure their weekly blood arrived from the harbour in carts bearing the governor’s symbol, and fed them animals in secret. Harlan never knew.
When Harlan beat her, the coven’s leader Isolde offered to “take care of this”, and Laura said yes.
The blood supply stopped a week or two ago, and the coven has gone feral since.



She is leaving the island to start again. Luna blessed her journey.

npcs/leon-thrace.title: Leon Thrace
npcs/leon-thrace.content:
Governor of Saltmere. Human, mid-twenties. Son of the late old governor and of Celandine, who died more than ten years ago.
What the party has seen

At the funeral (S24): He threw the nobles out of his father’s funeral, seated the commoners, made a speech about a new era and declared a town-wide celebration. Odettia lingered on his arm. Odettia also saw his eyes flash crimson.
His sickroom: Quinn and Milo found his old room in the manor’s medical wing: bloodstains, potions, and shackles on all four corners of the bed, with a hidden stair down to a dungeon of prisoners.
The key: Osric saw the Order of Aster key around Leon’s neck at the funeral. At dinner a chain around his neck disappeared under his shirt.
The invitation (S25): He wrote to the party: dinner, “come armed if it comforts you”, and a claim that he knows why his people are dying.
The dinner (S27):

He talked of a lifelong illness that left him bedridden until a house medic brought a cure from overseas.
He tends his late mother’s moonflowers himself, and her portrait is missing from the gallery.
He sealed the stair to the old dungeon after his father died.
He barely eats (“a liquid diet”), drinks only from his own cellar, and retires early because of his “poor constitution”.
He offered the party 800 gp to remove the coven he blames for eight deaths.
Asked by Quinn why he would kill his own kind: “I’m sure I don’t know what you mean.”


His politics: He describes his father’s rule as brutal and fear-driven, and says his father was a softer man before Leon’s mother died. “I want to give people something to work towards rather than something to run from.”

What the party wonders
Is he a vampire? His mother’s sister, Isolde, called him “that thing in there” and doubts he is her nephew at all. Odettia sensed something dormant in him. See open-threads.

npcs/milo-bramble.title: Milo Bramble
npcs/milo-bramble.content:
Halfling, sixteen. Eager and brave, and weighs about ninety pounds.

Baldur’s Gate (S12): He was a theatre helper at the Vellum Stage, hired by Aldric Mourne, and was unwittingly used as bait. The party rescued him, and he has been loyal to them ever since. He lived in a shack in the Outer City with a mattress and a lamp.
His mother: Marloes was freed from her Guild debt at sail-off (S15), through Odettia’s Guild favour, signed as “Morgan Duskbane”.
The voyage: The rigger Wren Talvas taught him to climb. He made his first kill in the sahuagin raid (S17).
Saltmere:

He infiltrated the manor with Quinn in borrowed priest’s robes (S24).
He works the taps for Gerta.
He nursed a hangover after a night on the spirits (S26).
At the governor’s table (S27) he came as Odettia’s ward in a borrowed tuxedo, with bare feet. He ate everything, then pocketed what he couldn’t eat, and politely declined Quinn’s invitation to the bathroom.

npcs/osric.title: Osric
npcs/osric.content:
Knight of the Order of Aster, and one of the seven companions who rode out with Vander’s father Umber and were never found at his death. Haggard, as if he has lived in the woods for days.

He tracked the Order’s stolen key to Saltmere alone, and saw it around Leon Thrace’s neck at the old governor’s funeral.
In S26 the party found him being savaged by the coven in the woods by Harlan’s farm. Vander saved and healed him, and Kaelith charmed him into telling the truth.
He saw Umber in Vander’s face. He fears Sundar, who he says has turned to Shar and is hunting the remaining members of Umber’s company, blaming them for their father’s death.
He took a room at the Green Leaf. In S27 he came in dazed, muttered “those bastards”, and stormed out again. The party doesn’t know where he went.

The party’s trust in him is fragile.

npcs/people-of-interest.title: People of Interest
npcs/people-of-interest.content:
People the party is chasing, being chased by, or worried about.
Sundar Duskbane
Vander’s older brother, once a steadfast paladin of Lathander, who left on an oath of vengeance after their father’s death. At the Closed Door (S13) Vander learned Sundar sold the stolen Order of Aster key; he “seemed certain” when he did. Zivra’s prophecy says he kneels to another god. In S26 Osric said Sundar has turned to Shar and is hunting what remains of Umber’s company. In S27 a manor guard mentioned rumours of a red-haired wanderer in the Moonshaes.
Morgan Duskbane
Vander’s twin sister, a fierce fighter still with the Order of Aster. She led the call to cast Vander out.
”M.D.”
Wrote to Castellar about the key and was heading to Baldur’s Gate.
Umber Duskbane
Vander’s father, a mighty paladin of Lathander. He was found dead outside Waterdeep, still gripping the key; the seven knights who rode with him vanished. Osric is one of them.
Aldric Mourne
The WSS’s operative in Baldur’s Gate: posh and human, by Milo’s account. He worked out of an Outer City building with a magical ward, and hired Milo at the Vellum Stage. The buyer’s agent for the key at the Closed Door also called himself “Mourne”. Cassia’s letter narrowed the man behind the alias to four candidates, including the brothers Erstin and Renard Holloway. The party overheard the name “Holloway” in Baldur’s Gate tied to Amn–Waterdeep politics, and Neve recalled Renard Holloway being linked to negotiations.
The Gundwynds and Deryc
The Waterdeep hippogriff-breeding family that Odettia was promised into, connected to the Black Boars. At the governor’s dinner (S27) a guard mentioned a Gundwynd trader due in Saltmere in a few days.
The Black Boars
A Baldur’s Gate gang hunting Odettia. Odettia and Kaelith fought two of them (S13) and watched them lean on Theron (S14).
Kannoth
The vampire lord whose undead hold fallen Cendriane. Kaelith barely escaped him.

npcs/saltmere-townsfolk.title: Saltmere Townsfolk
npcs/saltmere-townsfolk.content:
Major figures have their own pages: Leon Thrace · Isolde · Henrietta · Corv · Osric · Gerta Wrack · Edrik Cole · Laura · Yara Dunwell
Celandine
Leon’s mother and the old governor’s wife, called the governess. She died twelve years ago; the town was never told how. In Odettia’s vision she lay murdered in a torchlit dungeon with a wound across her chest. Her portrait is missing from the manor gallery. Moonflowers and sea bass were her favourites. She was Isolde’s sister: a tapestry hidden in the manor names them both. Her last letter to Isolde reads: “He knows. Keep the boy safe if I can’t.”
The old governor
Leon’s father, buried in S24. He ruled by fear, with punishments, whippings and hangings. Henrietta says his cruelty began about when the governess died. Leon says he was softer before. He died of illness after working himself into the ground. He signed the standing order letting manor wagons pass the docks uninspected.
Harlan
A Saltmere farmer, and not the same person as Harlan of the Loose Rigger in Baldur’s Gate. His livestock were drained of blood. He was killed by the coven after beating his wife Laura, rose as a feral undead and was destroyed by Vander (S25). He is buried under the oak by his fence.
Brennick
A foreign hunter who came to Saltmere decades ago, asked about the old ruling family, went up the manor road and never came back. Gerta remembers the mark stitched on his gear: two crossed lines through a closed eye, the same mark as in Quinn’s book. Cole’s arrival record lists him as “hunter” of the Talen family, and notes “no departure recorded”.
The Father
Saltmere’s elderly, slow-moving chapel priest, known simply as “Father”. Odettia effectively ran the old governor’s funeral for him. Vampire bites are his old speciality, and he knows how to cure Odettia’s (S27).
Voss
One of Leon’s guards. He warned the party about drawing weapons at dinner and has heard of “a red-haired wanderer” elsewhere in the Moonshaes. The party has now met several people named Voss: the tavern owner Sable Voss, and Ser Callum Voss, Marianne’s former owner.
Sable Voss
Keeps a tavern in town.
Fenna
A mother whose feverish son Kaelith cured with marshmallow leaf (S25). She named her “Kaelith the Wise”.
Cole’s office and the docks
See Edrik Cole.

npcs/sword-coast-people.title: People of the Sword Coast
npcs/sword-coast-people.content:
Daggerford and Bearbarrow
Priya Nagorth

A tiefling merchant who hauls goods along the Sword Coast. The party escorted her wagon out of Daggerford. Something in her cargo, a strongbox marked WSS, turned out to be far more dangerous than she knew.
Losandra Ayling

A tall orc, the constable of Bearbarrow and its only law. The party convinced her that the stable hand had been replaced by an ooze creature. Odettia has written to her and is still waiting for a reply.
Isaac Townsend

The jovial red-haired dwarf who keeps Bearbarrow’s inn.
Julius

Bearbarrow’s teenage stable hand, with a red scarf. He was taken and replaced by the oblex.
Bram Hallow
Losandra’s deputy. A creature dragged him into the mine beneath Edda Fenlow’s house, and he woke the next morning insisting that someone must be told the name Aldric.
Edda Fenlow
A Bearbarrow gardener who vanished from her farm the morning after the wagon arrived. Her cellar hid a path into the old mine.
Ferris and Cade Holt

Halfling brothers and petty criminals, held in Losandra’s cell. They were paid to cause a disturbance at the inn so that Julius could reach the wagon, and they swear they knew nothing more.
Tomas Geld, Denny and the Voss family
Tomas Geld is Bearbarrow’s dwarf carpenter, who lost a whole day of memory to the oblex. Denny is the baker, who wants proper walls. Marta Voss was replaced by a copy, which the party destroyed. Her mother-in-law, Old Petra Voss, had known for two days that it was not Marta.
Sister Wren

A travelling healer who arrived in Bearbarrow a few days before the wagon, selling remedies from a cart in the square. She heard people running to the well in the night.
The road south
The gnome on the road

A gnome with a cart, met on the road south of Bearbarrow. His name is not recorded.
Morvin and Rilla Kettlebottom
Halfling siblings who sell candles and soap along the Sword Coast, and argue about which inn has the best beds. Vander bought candles from them.
Zivra

The fortune-teller at the carnival who gave three of the party their prophecies (S8).
Gordo Plank

A relics dealer on the road into the Fields of the Dead, whose mule Duchess will not cross after dark. His relics are fake, but his warning about the Fields was not.
Harsk
A retired Flaming Fist soldier turned turnip farmer, stranded at the ford with other travellers by a wyvern (S9).
Cassia

A former Waterdeep City Watch investigator, Cassia Torn, who rode into Bearbarrow at Priya’s call and travelled south with the party. Briefed the party on the WSS (S10). Her letter at sea (S16) narrowed “Aldric Mourne” down to four men, two of them the brothers Erstin and Renard Holloway.
Aldren Thace
His letter reached the party in S10, and Vander delivered it to Brother Callum in Baldur’s Gate.
Baldur’s Gate
Theron Vale

The Belabranta family steward, a half-elf with a military bearing, and Odettia’s childhood tutor. He posted a 500 gp reward for her. She confronted him in disguise (S11), and the party later watched the Black Boars threaten him (S14).
Orin Castellar

Owner of the Closed Door, an invitation-only antiques showroom in the Upper City. Through him the party learned Sundar sold the Order of Aster key (S13). Kaelith bought a Cendriane emerald there.
Others

Bessa Ironhand: keeper of the Lizard’s Cradle, the party’s base, where Vander holds the stew record (8 bowls).
Thalwick: bookseller on the Basilisk Gate, who sold the party a book (S15).
Brother Callum: Shrine of the Moonmaiden.
Harlan of the Loose Rigger: a harbour-bar contact, and not Saltmere’s farmer.
Dane Copperweight: a jeweller whose cellar the party cleared (S14). It connects to the sewers, and he now believes someone matching Odettia fled down there.
Edren Gale: a wizard who teleported to the Black Boars’ hideout (S14).
Crane: a Black Boars figure.
Marloes: Milo’s mother.

At sea
Reza Sahil
The pirate whose three contests the party took on (S18): a drawn duel, the befriending of Biscuit, and a card game Odettia won. The prizes included a replacement chart and the greatsword Marianne, taken from Ser Callum Voss.

npcs/the-maris.title: The Maris and Her Crew
npcs/the-maris.content:
The ship that carried the party from Baldur’s Gate to the Moonshaes (S15–S23). It has since left Saltmere.
Neve Saren

Captain, about seventy, a retired sailor who inherited the Maris from her father, the last of a sailing family. She has sailed past Viledel some forty times and had never seen its lighthouse dark. She carries a debt on the ship that came to light in Saltmere (S23). She wears an emerald necklace that Kaelith recognised as Cendriane work, and it grew warm during Kaelith’s fading in the storm. She was washed overboard in that storm and rescued by the party (Kaelith in shark form, Vander hauling her in). In S25 she delivered Odettia’s parents’ letter to the Green Leaf on a night visit, then left on an errand to a southern island.
Bran Korr

The cook: a half-orc in his late fifties who has not spoken in twenty years. He talks with gestures, a slate and very expressive eyebrows. He is gentle, slips extra food to whoever looks worst, makes excellent pastries, and carves little wooden animals. At the drowned wreck (S19) he collapsed sobbing, and a cache of his carvings was found aboard. By the end of the kraken escape he seemed steadier than he had in years.
Wren Talvas

The rigger: early twenties, from Amn, four years aboard, and she lives in the crow’s nest. Chatty, optimistic, never surprised. She fled her own wedding the night before and won’t talk about it. She took Milo under her wing and taught him to climb the rigging.
Quinn
Found in the hold during the voyage. See Quinn.

npcs/yara-dunwell.title: Yara Dunwell
npcs/yara-dunwell.content:
Herbalist and apothecary of Saltmere, nearly twenty years in the trade. Short, with sleeves pushed up and forearms stained two colours. She is better at bookkeeping and customers than at growing things, by her own account.
Her drying herbs hang in twinkling bubbles of preservation magic, words taught to her by a frost-covered traveller whose life she saved: Corv. Near that magic, Kaelith feels solid in time. Corv returns to drain it to stay whole.
She hired Kaelith for a day (S25), sells her hangover cure (“Antivomix”, 50% to Kaelith), and charged a sick child’s mother only a copper. “Anytime you want to make a few bucks…”

open-threads.title: Open Threads
open-threads.content:
Urgent

Odettia’s bite: about three days left. The cure needs Isolde destroyed or her willing release; an item tied to Isolde (Odettia plans to ask Henrietta); and the chapel priest’s rite. Isolde will release her in exchange for Celandine’s letter.
Leon’s offer: answer due. 800 gp (300 up front, 500 on completion) to remove the coven. The party asked for one night.
Noon at Harlan’s farm? Quinn proposed meeting Isolde there the day after the dinner. She didn’t answer.

Saltmere

What is beneath the manor? Corv’s vial points down. The dungeon holds fifteen prisoners, and its east-wing stair has been nailed shut.
What is Leon? He drinks from his own cellar, barely eats, and his eyes flashed crimson. Isolde says “that thing in there” may not be her nephew, and Odettia sensed something dormant in him. Odettia’s Clairvoyance on his desk: what did she see?
Who killed Celandine, and why? “He knows. Keep the boy safe if I can’t.” Cole’s notes say “inside job?”
Henrietta and Isolde. Odettia promised Henrietta the truth, and Isolde wants a life with her.
The blood shipments. Who paid for twelve years of harbour blood in governor’s carts, and why did it stop?
The dead vampire. The guards say they killed one; the body is being held. And a second sighting that same night.
Brennick. The Talen hunter who went up the manor road and never came back.
The Tideworth’s cargo. Leon offered to tell what he knows if the party helps.
Osric. He stormed off muttering “those bastards”. Where did he go?
Cole’s missing documents. Sooner or later he will notice.

Wider world

Sundar has turned to Shar and is hunting Umber’s company. There are rumours of a red-haired wanderer in the Moonshaes.
The Gundwynds. A Gundwynd trader is due in Saltmere within days.
Aldric Mourne and the Holloways. Which of the four men is he?
Kaelith’s fading, and Cendriane.
The spiderweb coins and the kraken spawn, still out at sea.
Losandra’s reply to Odettia’s letter.

places/cendriane.title: Cendriane
places/cendriane.content:
The eladrin city of Kaelith’s birth, in the Feywild: a city of the elves’ great age, and Kaelith’s home some twelve thousand years ago. It fell in the war between the eladrin and the drow, just after her parents’ spell sent her forward in time. Today it is overrun by undead under the vampire lord Kannoth. Kaelith tried to return once and barely escaped.

A crossing point lies in eladrin ruins on the Sword Coast, found by Kaelith in S10. The ruins’ writing calls it a gate. She also heard tales of another crossing at the site of her ancient village, which the vampire lord now holds.
Cendriane emeralds are worn by her people’s descendants, as her mother’s jewellery and Captain Neve Saren’s necklace show. The emerald Kaelith bought in Baldur’s Gate crumbled to dust in the storm (S16), and her fading stopped.

places/index.title: Places
places/index.content:
Saltmere: the Moonshae harbour town where the party is now, with the manor, the Green Leaf, the Tailored Needle, the apothecary, the harbour and Harlan’s farm
The Sword Coast: Daggerford, Bearbarrow, the road south, Baldur’s Gate and Waterdeep
The voyage west: the storm, the wreck, the kraken spawn and the Viledel lighthouse
Cendriane: Kaelith’s lost city

places/saltmere.title: Saltmere
places/saltmere.content:
A small harbour town in the Korinn Archipelago of the Moonshae Isles, governed from a walled manor on the hill. It smells of tar, wet rope, fish guts and woodsmoke, with gulls loud over the quay. The docks are the only way in or out. The party arrived in S23, just as the old governor was buried, and found the town still celebrating days later under its new governor, Leon Thrace.

The manor

A walled hilltop estate with a formal garden, an apple orchard behind it and one main gatehouse.
What the party has seen inside:

Medical wing (S24): a working infirmary for townsfolk. Off it is the young lord’s old room: bloodstains on the stones, potions everywhere, and shackles on all four bed corners. A loose brick hides a spiral stair down.
Portrait gallery (S27): generations of governors, and a pale gap where Leon’s mother’s portrait hung.
East wing (S27): a door to the old dungeon stair, nailed shut by Leon.
Rooftop conservatory (S27): Leon’s moonflowers and his paper-strewn desk.
Dining hall (S27): a round table, a hundred-candle chandelier on a chain from the upper gallery, stained-glass windows, a great hearth. Doors lead to the garden balcony, the kitchens and the hallway.
A quiet side room (S27): holds a tapestry of two crowned women, named Celandine and Isolde.


The governor’s table (S27).
The hidden passage and dungeon
From the young lord’s room, a spiral stair runs about ten minutes down to a cold, torchlit tunnel with cart tracks. It passes a row of cells: ten empty and bloodstained, scratched with tallies and initials, and one holding fifteen shackled prisoners (S24). The tunnel runs on to the storehouse by the quay and has been heavily guarded since the break-in. In S27 Kaelith’s vial pointed down, toward whatever lies beneath the manor.
The storehouse

Near the quay, where the tunnel comes up. Its guardian, a dormant orb that unfolded into a four-metre speaking sentinel, was destroyed by Vander and Kaelith (S24). A desk ledger logged carts in and out over the last two weeks (taken by Vander).
The Green Leaf
The party’s base: a boarding house with a hand-painted sign, warm windows, cheap rooms, good stew and a job board, run by Gerta Wrack and her three arms. Milo works the taps. Osric took a room here.
The Tailored Needle
Henrietta’s shop on Ropewalk Lane: bolts of cloth, garments in the window, and a smell of beeswax, new wool and mothballs.
Yara Dunwell’s apothecary

Herbs dry in bubbles of preservation magic along the shop front. It smells of chamomile, tallow and vinegar. See Yara Dunwell.
The harbour and the harbourmaster’s office
Edrik Cole’s domain: ledgers, a locked oak cabinet, and the manifests of every crate. “Wine” bound for Harlan’s farm turned out to be blood.
The chapel

A chapel and graveyard, where the old governor’s funeral was held (S24) and where the priest who can cure Odettia’s bite sits over his stew.
Harlan’s farm
About a mile out along the main road: a stone house and slate-roofed barn above a sea cliff. Harlan lies buried under the oak by the fence. A hidden hatch in the farmhouse leads to the coven’s lair: hundreds of empty blood bottles, a tapestry of two crowned women, and years of animal bones behind it. A belt of woods lies to the north, where the Order of Aster’s symbol is carved into a tree and where the party fought the coven (S26).
The ruins to the north
Where Corv shelters.
Elsewhere in town
The market square, a forge and a jeweller (visited S23), and Sable Voss’s tavern.

places/sword-coast.title: The Sword Coast
places/sword-coast.content:
Daggerford

Where the adventure began (Sessions 1–5). The town had been reinforced by Waterdeep amid rising tension with Amn. Here the party answered a call for caravan guards. The full story of these first sessions is on early-sessions.

Bearbarrow

A small village on the road, where Priya Nagorth’s wagon stopped for the night (Sessions 6–7). Something got out of her cargo, replaced the stable hand Julius, and slipped down the well. The party exposed the impostor to Constable Losandra Ayling, cleared the old mine beneath the village, and found the WSS strongbox.

































Julius, the stable handIsaac Townsend, the innkeeperLosandra Ayling, the constablePriya Nagorth and her wagonSister WrenThe halfling brothers
The road south

A gnome with a cart and two halfling candle-sellers, then the carnival Marvelo’s Magnificent Midway, where Zivra read three fortunes (S8). The Fields of the Dead are a valley of cairns, the graves of the Waterdeep and Amn armies from the battle of the Winding River. Beyond them, an old watchtower by a ford was the roost of a wyvern, until a griffon returned to it and woke Odettia’s amulet (S9). Eladrin ruins, almost entirely underground, holding a crossing point toward Cendriane (S10).
Baldur’s Gate


Outer City: the Lizard’s Cradle (the party’s base, kept by Bessa Ironhand; Vander’s stew record); Aldric Mourne’s warded building; the Basilisk Gate market, with Thalwick’s Books; Dane Copperweight’s jewellery shop, whose cellar breaks into the sewers; Milo’s shack; a Black Boars tavern.
Lower City: the Loose Rigger harbour bar, the docks, and the Vellum Stage theatre where the party found Milo.
Upper City: the Closed Door (Orin Castellar’s invitation-only antiques showroom) and the Shrine of the Moonmaiden. Getting in takes persuasion or a bribe.

Waterdeep
Home of the Belabrantas, the Gundwynds, the Order of Aster’s Spires of the Morning, a church of Selûne, and the WSS.

places/the-sea.title: The Voyage West
places/the-sea.content:
The Maris sailed from Baldur’s Gate at dawn (S15), chasing the Tideworth toward the Moonshae Isles. A crossing meant to take days took weeks.

The storm (S16): Kaelith faded nearly to the elbow, Neve went overboard, and Odettia’s wings became known.
Sahuagin raid (S17): a night attack led by a priestess. The raiders left coins stamped with a spiderweb and a fish head. Milo made his first kill.
Sabotage and drift (S18): the chart was burned and the compass fouled. A stowaway, Quinn, was found in the hold. The pirate Reza Sahil and his three contests.
The wreck on the sandbank (S19): the coins grew warmer as the ship approached a grounded Waterdeep navy wreck. Its drowned crew rose against the party. Aboard they found a ship’s log of a Moonshae mission some fifteen years back, a cap of water breathing, and a cache of Bran’s carved animals. Below lay a fish-headed idol. Then the sea drained back and a kraken spawn’s tentacle rose.
Escape (S20): four desperate rounds. The kraken spawn dragged the wreck under and let them go.

Viledel Lighthouse

A lighthouse on a lonely isle that Neve had never seen dark in forty passings. It was dark. The party destroyed an allip on the approach (S20), then a dread wight and a dread wraith inside, and relit the beacon (S21). Quinn looked into the lighthouse orb mid-fight and was struck senseless, the start of his Orb Curse. A keeper’s diary mentioned the Tideworth.

The top of the lighthouse.
From Viledel it was two more days to Saltmere (S22).

sessions/early-sessions.title: Daggerford to the Fields of the Dead (Sessions 1–10)
sessions/early-sessions.content:
These sessions were not recorded. This page is rebuilt from the DM’s own notes and the pictures shown at the table, so it is lighter than the later write-ups. If something here is wrong or missing, tell the DM.
Daggerford (Sessions 1–5)

The campaign opened on the first day of Tarsakh. Waterdeep had reinforced Daggerford because of rising tension with Amn, which feared an attack. The party answered a call for caravan guards (the poster is in the gallery) and took a contract from the tiefling merchant Priya Nagorth: escort her wagon of goods along the Sword Coast. Among the cargo was a strongbox stamped with the initials WSS. Priya did not know what was inside it.
Before the wagon left, each character spent a couple of hours preparing for the journey. The road out of Daggerford held several incidents: a flooded road, a woman feigning distress while her partner tried to rob the party, and a caravan inspection as they left the city. Beyond that, nothing survives in the notes.
Bearbarrow (Sessions 6–7)

The first night. Dusk found the wagon at Bearbarrow, a small village on the road, and the party took rooms at Isaac Townsend’s inn. Later that night they heard a sharp crash and a muffled scream from behind the tavern, where the wagon was parked. In the yard lay a shattered jar and the stable hand’s red scarf, with a trail of ooze and blood leading from the wagon to the village well. The session ended as something slipped into the well.
The morning after. Julius, the stable hand, walked into the tavern at breakfast, healthy and cheerful. The party did not believe it. They persuaded Constable Losandra Ayling that “Julius” was really an ooze creature wearing his face. Her deputy Bram Hallow reported that the gardener Edda Fenlow had not turned up for work. Her house looked ordinary, but a hidden path led from the cellar into an old mine. In the tunnel something pale and slick seized Bram and dragged him into the dark. The party chased it through a collapsing passage, fought the spawn of Julius and Edda in the first chamber, and climbed back out.
Rounding up the village. Back above ground the party worked with Losandra to account for everyone:

Ferris and Cade Holt, halfling brothers, sat in the village cell. They had been paid to start a disturbance at the inn that night so that Julius could reach the wagon unwatched. They did not know what was in the strongbox or what had happened to Julius afterwards.
Priya had gone through her papers and laid three documents on the inn table: her contract (marked with a stylised eye inside a circle, the WSS mark), a manifest for “one sealed research container, handle with care”, and a letter hidden in the strongbox’s false bottom, addressed to “the Society” and signed Aldric. It spoke of a “secondary site” being prepared. Priya, who had carried goods up and down the coast for years, asked: “Was I carrying something alive?”
Tomas Geld, the dwarf carpenter, was found at his farm with ooze on him. It slid off as the party came near. He had lost a whole day of memory, “like a floor where a staircase used to be”.
Denny, the baker, came when summoned and complained about the lack of walls. Sister Wren, a travelling healer with a cart in the square, had heard people running toward the well in the night.
Marta Voss had been replaced as well. The party and Losandra confronted the copy at the house on the west lane and destroyed it. Marta’s mother-in-law Old Petra Voss, bedridden, had known for two days that it was not her Marta. Losandra, who had known Marta for thirty years, told her gently that Marta was gone.

The night in the inn. Vander gave a speech to the gathered villagers, they raised their glasses, and everyone slept.
The second morning. Fresh horse tracks in the mud showed that a rider had sat at the south tree line for two hours in the night, watching the inn, then left before dawn. Bram woke and said only one thing: “Aldric. Tell someone: Aldric.” Minutes later Cassia Torn, Priya’s contact, rode in. She read the tracks as a scout, not a team, with the team half a day behind. She also gave the party a name and an address: Aldric Mourne, in Baldur’s Gate’s Outer City.
The mine. The party went back down through Edda’s cellar. The old Corwick silver mine ran down through an assay room full of forty-year-old records, a passage of alcoves where the oblex kept the stolen voices of the people it had taken, and a flooded shaft, to the oblex in its deepest chamber. Some of the voices in the alcoves were scraps of the party’s own memories. Cassia did not go down with them. The party destroyed the oblex with fire. Priya, shaken, decided to carry on to Baldur’s Gate to find Aldric Mourne, and Cassia travelled with them.
See oblexes-and-the-wss for what an oblex is and what the party knows of the WSS.
The road south (Session 8)

The wagon headed south with Priya driving and Cassia silent in the back.

A gnome with a cart stopped the party on the road. (He is the “gnome on the road” in the gallery; the DM does not remember his name.)
Morvin and Rilla Kettlebottom, halfling siblings who sell hand-dipped candles and soap between towns, sat on a boulder at a crossroads sharing bread and cheese while arguing about which inn on the road has the best beds. They tried to recruit the party to either side, and to sell them candles; Vander bought some.
Marvelo’s Magnificent Midway: a small carnival in a meadow off the road, with violet and gold wagons and lantern lines. Its ringmaster, Madame Zivra, a tiefling in a violet coat and a crooked top hat, could not stop making puns. Games cost 2 copper and paid brass prize tokens; the party played every game on the midway, including arm wrestling against a half-orc tent rigger (the “arm-wrestling orc” in the gallery).
In her tent Zivra gave Kaelith, Odettia and Vander the three prophecies. The wagon rolled on into the evening in near silence.

The Fields of the Dead (Session 9)

Gordo Plank, a weathered man with a mule named Duchess, sold “genuine artifacts of the Fields of the Dead”: rusty swords, a dented helmet and a bent arrowhead that he said had killed a famous general, each with its own grand story. When the party took him seriously he dropped the act and warned them: cross in daylight, stay on the road, never camp between the cairns, and if you hear voices, “it’s the wind”.
The Fields themselves are a vast, flat valley of cairns, the graves of the armies of Waterdeep and Amn that fought at the Winding River about two hundred years ago. One cairn is taller than the rest, with names carved in both languages. Cassia had crossed four times and never stayed for the night; Priya, six times, without looking.
On the road lay a dead ox with talon marks, a wrecked wagon, and a camp of stranded travellers at the ford led by Harsk, a retired Flaming Fist soldier. He said a young wyvern was nesting in the ruined watchtower beyond the crossing, and that the Fist patrols had been pulled into Baldur’s Gate, leaving the road unwatched. The party planned their approach, with Cassia’s crossbow in support, and killed the wyvern.

Odettia knew the iron perch rings on the tower wall: they were griffon fittings, the design her family uses at the Belabranta estate. After the fight a real griffon returned to its roost. It looked at Odettia, lowered its head, and let her stand near it. Her family amulet, the Griffontack, grew warm. The party crossed the ford and camped at the southern edge of the Fields, where Cassia mentioned a contact on the Baldur’s Gate docks named Harlan.
The ruins and Cassia’s briefing (Session 10)
The party reached eladrin ruins, almost entirely underground. Kaelith felt the traces of magic there were strong, and found writing describing the place as a gate. She also learned of tales of another crossing point, at the site of her ancient village, which is now held by the vampire lord (see cendriane). A woman named Thistle was there too. A drake ambush followed (the drakes and the cold camp are in the gallery), and during it a thief made off with the strongbox. The party never learned who it was and guessed the WSS. At the cold camp Cassia told them what she knew. The WSS was experimenting with oblexes in order to replace people of power. She had been investigating Aldric Mourne and had seven possible names for him, two of them the Holloway brothers. She also told them about the other oblex she had gone to investigate, and the sea cave north of Waterdeep where it was sealed. A pilgrim, Aldren Thace, gave Vander a letter for Brother Callum. From there the road led to Baldur’s Gate.

sessions/index.title: Session Log
sessions/index.content:
Session numbers follow the DM’s campaign record. On 1 October 2026 every session was renumbered +5 to count the five Daggerford sessions at the start. Older notes may use the old numbers.
The first ten sessions, with no recordings, are gathered on early-sessions. Sessions with a full page: 25 · 26 · 27.
Daggerford













#Session1–5Daggerford. The party gathers in Daggerford and takes a contract escorting Priya Nagorth’s wagon. No recordings or notes beyond the map and the caravan-guards poster in the gallery. See early-sessions.
Bearbarrow and the road south

























#Session6–7Bearbarrow. Something escapes Priya’s wagon and replaces the stable hand Julius: an oblex. The party exposes it, clears the mine below the village, and finds a strongbox marked WSS.8Road South. A carnival; the fortune-teller Zivra delivers three prophecies.9Fields of the Dead. A wyvern fight; a griffon at an old watchtower; the Griffontack awakens.10Eladrin Ruins. Kaelith finds a crossing point toward Cendriane. In a drake ambush a thief steals the strongbox. Cassia briefs the party on the WSS; a letter from Aldren Thace.
Baldur’s Gate





























#Session11Arrival in Baldur’s Gate. Theron Vale’s reward poster for Odettia. Shopping at the Basilisk Gate; Thace’s letter delivered to the Shrine of the Moonmaiden. Odettia confronts Theron in disguise.12Investigation. Leads from Harlan at the Loose Rigger about the Tideworth; a fight at the Vellum Stage; the party meets Milo and Neve Saren and overhears the name “Holloway”.13Three Heartbeats. At the Closed Door: Sundar sold the key, the buyer’s agent was “Mourne”, and a letter signed “M.D.” Odettia fights the Black Boars. Vander sets the stew record at the Lizard’s Cradle (8 bowls). Dreams.14The Last Day. Spying on Theron as the Black Boars lean on him; the wizard Edren Gale teleports to the Boars’ hideout. The party clears a jeweller’s cellar connected to the sewers and plants a false trail.15Sail-Off. Thalwick’s book bought. Milo’s mother Marloes freed from her Guild debt (Odettia signs as “Morgan Duskbane”). A coastal chart; a vision at Luna’s shrine. The Maris sails at dawn.
The voyage





































#Session16Storm at Sea. Cassia’s letter narrows “Aldric Mourne” to four men, including the brothers Erstin and Renard Holloway. Kaelith’s fading surges and her emerald crumbles, stopping it. Neve goes overboard and is rescued. Odettia’s wings become common knowledge.17Raiders in the Dark. A night sahuagin raid; Milo’s first kill; spiderweb and fish-head coins; a fog bank ahead.18The Chart and the Drift. The chart is burned and the compass fouled by an unknown saboteur. Quinn is found stowed away in the hold. Reza Sahil’s three contests (a drawn duel, Biscuit befriended, cards won); a replacement chart and the greatsword Marianne gained. Adrift.19The Wreck on the Sandbank. A planted lodestone removed from the compass. The coins lead to a drowned Waterdeep navy wreck; its dead crew fought. A ship’s log, a cap of water breathing, and Bran’s carvings found aboard. A kraken spawn surfaces.20The Dark Beacon. Escape from the kraken spawn. Crossing to dark Viledel; an allip destroyed.21Lighthouse Interiors. A dread wight and a dread wraith destroyed; the beacon relit. Quinn looks into the orb and is cursed. A keeper’s diary mentions the Tideworth.22Underway. Two days’ crossing from Viledel to Saltmere.
Saltmere





























#Session23The Better Man. Docking in Saltmere (a blank permit gets them past the harbourmaster). Neve’s debt revealed. Errands at the market, chapel, forge, jeweller and healer. News of the new governor, Leon Thrace, and the old governor’s funeral; the party splits three ways.24A Tomorrow Worth Trusting. Odettia runs the funeral from the inside. Quinn and Milo infiltrate the manor and find a hidden dungeon with fifteen prisoners. Vander and Kaelith destroy the storehouse guardian.25**The Ones Who Never Left.** Escape to the Green Leaf; Luna’s mount form; four solo jobs around town; the Isolde vision, Cole’s cabinet, Harlan risen, Corv; Leon’s invitation.26**The Coven.** Familiars spot the coven; a fight in the woods at Harlan’s farm; Osric rescued; the lair beneath the farm; a guarded truce.27**The Governor’s Table.** Laura’s confession; Odettia’s bite; dinner with Leon and his offer; Quinn meets Isolde; the vial points beneath the manor.

sessions/session-25.title: Session 25: The Ones Who Never Left
sessions/session-25.content:
Played over two nights. Previous: Session 24 · Next: Session 26
Night one: a roof over their heads

The party slipped out of the storehouse ahead of a manor patrol and found rooms at the Green Leaf, run by the three-armed dwarf Gerta Wrack. Vander helped her shift crates and paid for the first night.
Gerta’s gossip included a foreign hunter who came to Saltmere decades ago, asked about the old ruling family, went up the manor road and never came back. He carried a mark stitched on his gear: two crossed lines through a closed eye, the same mark as in the book that taught Quinn his shadow technique.
Quinn laid out a theory: Leon as a vampire, explaining his lifelong illness and sudden recovery, the bloodless livestock, the vanished hunter and the shackled prisoners. He let slip that he grew up in a vampire household. Vander came round to the idea.
Pressed by Vander, Odettia insisted nothing about Leon felt cold or wrong. But she had seen his eyes flash crimson when they met.
Neve Saren delivered a letter to Odettia from her parents.
In the street outside the inn, Luna grew into a towering, glowing, saddled mount for the first time.

Night two: four jobs, one day

Each player played a solo scene while the others waited outside. The four met again at the Green Leaf at sunset.
Odettia at the Tailored Needle

The seamstress Henrietta hired Odettia to mend festival clothes. Odettia turned out to have a gift for needlework and added an embroidered border of vines and flowers to a shirt (“I can make a fortune on that”). Henrietta mentioned that Cole the harbourmaster had seen a griffin over the sea the day before; Odettia’s griffin token warmed.
An owl flew in, took a pair of old velvet gloves from a chest Henrietta never opens, and gave them to Odettia. At their touch, Aerdrie Faenya sent her a vision, and for the first time Odettia stayed on her feet. She was looking through the eyes of the gloves’ owner: in a torchlit dungeon, a woman with dark pinned hair and a grey dress lay dead, ice cold, with a wound across her chest.
Henrietta said the gloves belonged to Isolde, her partner of ten years, who vanished one morning twelve years ago. From Odettia’s description, Henrietta recognised the dead woman as the governess, the lady of the manor and Leon’s mother. Isolde had been her handmaiden. The governess died twelve years ago and the town was never told how; the old governor’s cruelty began almost to the day.
Odettia promised Henrietta she would find the truth.

Quinn at the docks

Working for Harbourmaster Edrik Cole, Quinn learned:

Prisoners have long gone through the dock to the dungeons under the manor, and the numbers have jumped: twelve in a single day.
A shipment of animals for Harlan’s farm “never arrived”.
Prison and torture equipment was signed for by the head of the Manor Guard.


He tasted a bottle of “wine” bound for Harlan’s farm. It was blood.
A drained body was pulled from the harbour, with two fang punctures below the elbow: the mark of a restrained, elegant vampire.
While Cole was busy, Quinn picked his private cabinet:

Brennick’s decades-old arrival record, with the closed-eye mark and “no departure recorded”
a mortality register showing bursts of deaths, and three this week (taken)
a governor’s standing order, renewed for about thirty years, letting manor wagons pass uninspected
a large payment to the ship Tideworth, marked “agent”
Cole’s own notes on the governess’s death: “horrible death”, “body mutilated”, circled “inside job?” (taken)



Vander at Harlan’s farm

Dead cows lay where they had stood, bloodless and untouched by scavengers. In the barn lay Harlan himself, with clean punctures in the crook of his elbow. He rose red-eyed and feral, and Vander cut him down with radiant steel.
Upstairs, Harlan’s wife Laura tested Vander by cutting herself and watching him. She told him a red-eyed, clawed woman had seized Harlan the night before, told Laura to get back inside if she wanted to live, and seemed not to mean her harm.
Vander buried Harlan under the oak, with his lantern at the head of the grave in the custom of his order.
On the ride back, fresh horse tracks led into the trees, and the symbol of the Order of Aster was carved into a trunk. Vander called out. A four-note whistle answered, one he feels he should know.

Kaelith at Yara’s apothecary

Kaelith made hangover cures (“Antivomix”) for Yara Dunwell and cured a feverish boy with marshmallow leaf after Yara’s tonic failed. The boy’s mother, Fenna, named her “Kaelith the Wise.” Near Yara’s preservation magic, Kaelith felt solid and anchored for the first time in this age.
A ragged, frost-rimed man came in: Corv, the traveller Yara once saved. When he and Kaelith touched hands, both their arms turned translucent to the bone. He was thrown five years forward by a broken dragon-blood time spell and has been fading ever since.
He gave Kaelith a nearly finished cure, missing one ingredient: “the thing that does not die, the thing that consumes”, which he has traced to the manor. The vial will react when it is close. The deal: if she completes it, he uses it and teaches her to make her own.

Back at the Green Leaf

The four pooled what they had learned. Odettia revealed that her ancestor Ilithrea Belabranta, the name Corv had mentioned, slew a green dragon.
Kaelith found that Laura was hiding bruises and healed them. Harlan had been beating her.
A rider in manor colours brought a letter from Leon Thrace:

Dinner tomorrow at dusk. “Come armed if it comforts you.”
He owes one of them a debt from his father’s funeral.
Two of his people are dead this week, he knows why, and he can’t say so publicly.


They accepted. Vander will go as Odettia’s guard.

sessions/session-26.title: Session 26: The Coven
sessions/session-26.content:
Working title. Previous: Session 25 · Next: Session 27

Owls at night. Odettia’s owl Ariane and Kaelith’s new owl Barry scouted the woods by Harlan’s farm overnight. They saw a lone traveller being stalked by pale women.
The clearing. Vander, keeping his promise to Laura, rode out with Kaelith, and the party followed. In a clearing, three young vampires were tearing at a bloodied man while an older woman watched.

Vander recognised the man as a knight of his own Order, charged in to protect him and healed him.
Kaelith raised a wall of wind to part the fighters; the vampires ignored it.
Quinn fought from the shadows with psychic strikes.
Odettia grappled the coven’s leader to stop the violence. The leader bit her neck, and Odettia resisted her charm.
Vander struck the leader, then held back and knocked her unconscious instead of killing her. The other vampires stopped.


Osric. The man was Osric, one of the seven knights who rode with Vander’s father Umber. Kaelith charmed him into telling the truth:

He tracked the Order of Aster key to Saltmere, and saw it around Leon Thrace’s neck at the funeral.
He saw Umber in Vander’s face.
He fears Sundar, who he says has turned to Shar and is hunting the rest of Umber’s company, blaming them for their father’s death.


The truce. The coven’s leader said Osric drew first blood. She said her coven hunts “a greater evil” in the manor that wears a familiar face in town, and that chaos in the manor “would not be frowned upon”. She left as mist.
The lair. Quinn found a hidden hatch in the farmhouse leading to a basement: hundreds of empty blood bottles, a tapestry of two crowned women (one resembling the murdered governess), and animal bones Kaelith judged to be one to ten years old.
Before they left:

Through his psychic link, Quinn arranged a private meeting with the coven leader behind the manor the next evening (a “hot date”). Vander thinks it’s unsafe.
Vander took a bag of gold from the farmhouse chest for Laura.
Osric took a room at the Green Leaf.

sessions/session-27.title: Session 27: The Governor's Table
sessions/session-27.content:
Previous: Session 26
Before dinner


Quinn’s curse stirred, but he rolled a natural 20, boxed the intrusion up and set it aside for a while.


Osric had come to the Green Leaf an hour earlier, muttered “those bastards” and stormed back out.


Odettia’s bite. In the mirror: two closed punctures, cold skin, and fine black lines spreading along her veins. She isn’t turning yet, but if the lines pass the point she marked, symptoms begin. At the chapel the old priest said he can cure it on three conditions:

The vampire that bit her must be destroyed or willingly release her.
It must be done within three days at most.
He needs something tied to the attacker, ideally from where she rests.

Quinn followed her there, unseen.


Laura’s confession. Vander and Kaelith visited Laura, and Vander added 20 gold to her bag before she would talk. What she told them:

For twelve years a coven of frightened vampires has lived in her cellar. She sheltered them, fed them animals in secret, and made sure their weekly bottled blood arrived from the harbour, in carts bearing the governor’s symbol. Harlan never knew.
A few nights ago Harlan beat her. The coven came, and their leader, Isolde, asked, “Do you want me to take care of this?” Laura said yes.
Isolde said the last human she had wanted to kill was the old governor, twelve years ago.
The blood shipments stopped a week or two ago. Since then the coven has gone feral and hunts openly.

Laura is leaving the island. Luna gave her a parting blessing.


Dressing up. Odettia lent Kaelith a dark green velvet gown and conjured a red one for herself with her hat of disguise. Vander and Quinn went as they were. Milo came as Odettia’s ward, in a tuxedo borrowed from Gerta (no shoes).


The manor


Leon Thrace met them at the door: dark green coat, a chain around his neck vanishing under his shirt. His guards let them keep their weapons but warned that anyone who draws one dies. One guard is named Voss. Leon told them that cats have protected his house for generations, and stroked Luna.
The tour:

Portrait gallery. A pale gap between the old governor and Leon where his mother’s portrait hung. His father took it down soon after she died, more than ten years ago, when Leon was very young.
A nailed-shut door. The east-wing stair to the old dungeon, sealed by Leon after his father died, “for the better of the community”.
Rooftop conservatory and office. Moonflowers, his mother’s favourite, which he tends himself; Kaelith judged them flawlessly cared for. A lifelong illness kept him bedridden until the house medic brought a cure from overseas. His father died of illness after running himself into the ground. Odettia’s magical senses caught only faint threads of something dormant in him.


Leon’s philosophy. Pain should be acknowledged and put right, not memorialised. His father ruled by fear and was a softer man before Leon’s mother died.

Dinner


The table. A round table (“so we converse as equals”), six guards, a hundred-candle chandelier. Courses of broth, then sea bass, his mother’s favourite. Her name was Celandine.
Small details:

A guard mentioned a Gundwynd trader due in a few days.
Leon barely ate; he says his illness left him on a liquid diet. His glass was filled only from “his lordship’s cellar wine”. Quinn thought he smelled iron somewhere in the room.


Leon’s request. Seven townspeople killed in two weeks, drained of blood. One was the captain of the guard, three days ago. His guards would be “fodder”. On his first day as governor he sent a negotiator to the coven, and they sent back his head. He offered 800 gp (300 up front) to remove the coven. He also offered to tell the party what he knows about the Tideworth’s cargo if they help.
An eighth victim was reported during dinner. Later a guard announced they had trapped a vampire in a fortified building and shot her from the rafters. Odettia asked that the body be kept.
The party asked for a night to decide. Leon retired at eleven because of his “poor constitution”. When Quinn asked why he would kill his own kind, Leon said, “I’m sure I don’t know what you mean.”

Quinn’s errand

Slipping out unseen, Quinn found a quiet room with the same tapestry as in the farm cellar, this time with names stitched beneath: Celandine and Isolde. Along the hem: “Sister for sister, thread for thread, pull the name of the one not wed.” Pulling the thread of Isolde’s name opened a hidden pocket:

Celandine’s last letter to her sister: “He knows. Keep the boy safe if I can’t. Love, your sister.”
a travel bag with 100 gp and survival tools


In the orchard he met Isolde. “You walk quietly, little hunter… someone with fangs, I think.”

She wants a life with Henrietta, but the town hunts her every night.
“They killed my sister in front of me.” She holds everyone in the manor complicit.
She asked Quinn to open the orchard door to let her in. He refused.
She offered to release Odettia from the bite in exchange for Celandine’s letter. Quinn kept the letter for now.
When Quinn called Leon her nephew, she laughed: “You think that thing in there is my nephew?… That is the one question I would love the answer to.”
She will consult her coven, and warned that if Quinn crosses her, he’ll be the first she kills. He proposed meeting at Harlan’s farm at noon tomorrow; she didn’t answer.



Midnight

Odettia secretly cast Clairvoyance on Leon’s desk in the conservatory. What she saw or heard is still to come.
As the clock struck midnight, Kaelith’s hand turned translucent again. In her pack, Corv’s vial shook violently, its contents pooling downward, toward whatever lies beneath the manor.
Guards cut the evening short (a second vampire sighting in town) and saw everyone out. On the way, Voss mentioned rumours of a red-haired wanderer elsewhere in the Moonshaes.

In the carriage
The party argued it through:

Is Leon a vampire, something else entirely, or even an oblex?
Why did the coven only turn violent once the old governor died and the blood stopped?
Should they bring Leon and Isolde face to face?

Odettia felt no bond break, so the vampire the guards killed wasn’t the one who bit her. The likeliest plan is a return to the dungeons through the tunnel. Leon is still waiting for an answer.

story-so-far.title: The Story So Far
story-so-far.content:
Daggerford and the wagon (Sessions 1–5)
The adventure began in Daggerford, a town reinforced by Waterdeep amid rising tension with Amn. The party took work escorting the wagon of the tiefling merchant Priya Nagorth. There are no recordings from these early days; see early-sessions for what the DM’s notes preserve, and the gallery for the map of Daggerford and the poster that started it.
Bearbarrow (Sessions 6–7)
On the road, Priya’s wagon stopped at the village of Bearbarrow. Something escaped from her cargo in the night: an oblex, an ooze that steals memories and wears people’s faces. It replaced the stable hand Julius. The party exposed the impostor to the constable, cleared the mine beneath the village, and found a strongbox marked WSS.
The road south (Sessions 8–10)
At a carnival the fortune-teller Zivra gave Odettia, Vander and Kaelith each a prophecy. The party fought a wyvern, and at an old watchtower Odettia’s family amulet, the Griffontack, woke. In eladrin ruins Kaelith found a crossing point toward her lost home, Cendriane. During a drake ambush, a thief made off with the WSS strongbox; the party guessed the WSS but never learned who. Afterwards Cassia briefed the party on the WSS.
Baldur’s Gate (Sessions 11–15)
In Baldur’s Gate they found Odettia’s face on a reward poster put up by her family’s steward, Theron Vale. They traced the WSS’s local operative, Aldric Mourne, to an Outer City building and a theatre, the Vellum Stage. There they rescued young Milo and overheard the name Holloway.
At an antiques house called the Closed Door, Vander learned the worst: his brother Sundar had sold the stolen Order of Aster key. The buyer’s agent called himself “Mourne”, and the key left west aboard a ship, the Tideworth. Someone signing only “M.D.” had written asking about it too, and was heading for Baldur’s Gate.
The party dodged the Black Boars gang hunting Odettia and laid a false trail. They freed Milo’s mother from a Guild debt, then sailed at dawn on Captain Neve Saren’s ship, the Maris, after the Tideworth.
The voyage (Sessions 16–22)
A storm nearly took Kaelith, whose body began to fade, and Neve went overboard and was rescued. Sahuagin raided the ship by night, leaving strange spiderweb coins. Someone burned the chart and fouled the compass. A stowaway, Quinn, was found in the hold.
The pirate Reza Sahil challenged the party to three contests, and they came away with a new chart and the greatsword Marianne. The coins led them to a drowned Waterdeep navy wreck, its dead crew, and a kraken spawn they barely escaped. At the dark Viledel lighthouse they destroyed a dread wight and a dread wraith and relit the beacon. Quinn looked into the lighthouse’s orb and has carried a curse ever since.
Saltmere (Sessions 23–27)
They reached Saltmere, a harbour town in the Moonshaes, just as its old governor was buried. His son Leon Thrace threw out the nobles, seated the commoners and declared a celebration.
While Odettia ran the funeral from inside, Quinn and Milo slipped into the manor. They found Leon’s old sickroom, with shackles on the bed, and a hidden stair down to a dungeon with fifteen chained prisoners. Vander and Kaelith destroyed a guardian construct in the harbour storehouse that the tunnel leads to.
The next day the party split up for jobs around town, and every thread pointed back in time:

a hunter who arrived decades ago and never left
a thirty-year order letting manor wagons pass the docks unchecked
harbour “wine” that was really blood
a governess murdered twelve years ago

At Harlan’s farm Vander destroyed the farmer’s risen corpse. Kaelith met Corv, a man fading out of time as she is. And Leon invited them to dinner.
